messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi there! I’ve been having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I can send regular texts just fine, but whenever I try to send a picture or a group message, it doesn’t go through. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?

I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to verify your identity and identify the phone line you’re having trouble with. Could you please provide your full name and date of birth, or the phone number associated with the line experiencing the MMS issue?
Sure thing! My name is John Smith, and the phone number with the issue is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any other information from me.

{"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 15.1, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": true, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}

Thank you for the information, John. I’ve confirmed your account and identified the line associated with 555-123-2002 as active.

To troubleshoot your MMS issue, I’ll need to check a few things about your device and network settings. Could you please let me know if you’re able to use mobile data (for example, browsing the web when Wi-Fi is off)? Also, are you currently connected to Wi-Fi or using mobile data when trying to send MMS messages?
(guides the customer through a device action)
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.
(guides the customer through a device action)
Status Bar: 📶³ Good | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’m currently not connected to Wi-Fi—Wi-Fi is turned off. My phone shows that mobile data is enabled, and I have a good signal with 5G coverage. Would you like me to try anything specific to test if my mobile data is working, like browsing a website?

Yes, that would be helpful! Please try browsing a website or using an app that requires internet access (with Wi-Fi still off) to confirm that your mobile data is working. Let me know if you’re able to access the internet, or if you encounter any issues. This will help us determine if the problem is specific to MMS or if it’s related to your mobile data connection in general.
(guides the customer through a device action)
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running a speed test with Wi-Fi still off, but it failed and said there’s no connection. It looks like my mobile data might not be working properly. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since your mobile data isn’t working, that would explain why MMS messages aren’t going through—MMS requires a mobile data connection.

Let’s start by checking if your phone’s mobile data is actually enabled at the system level. Could you please check your phone’s status bar and confirm if you see a mobile data icon (like 5G, 4G, LTE, etc.)? Also, do you see any icons indicating Airplane Mode is on, or any other unusual symbols?

If you’re not sure, I can guide you through checking your phone’s network status. Would you like step-by-step instructions for that?

Looking at my status bar, I can see a 5G icon and an icon that shows mobile data is enabled. I don’t see anything indicating Airplane Mode is on, and there aren’t any unusual symbols that I notice.

Is there anything specific you’d like me to check next, or would you like me to follow any particular steps?

Great, thanks for confirming that. Since your status bar shows 5G and mobile data enabled, but your speed test still fails, the next step is to check if your SIM card is being recognized correctly by your phone. Sometimes, SIM issues can cause data problems even if the signal looks good.

Could you please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings? If you’d like, I can guide you through the steps to check if your SIM card is active, missing, or locked. Would you like instructions for this?
(guides the customer through a device action)
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked the SIM card status—my SIM card is active and appears to be working properly. What would you like me to try next?

Thank you for checking your SIM card status. Since your SIM is active and your status bar shows 5G with mobile data enabled, but you still have no data connection, the next likely cause is an issue with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent mobile data and MMS from working.

Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks unusual or if you see an error? If you’re unsure, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings to default, which often resolves this type of issue. Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings?
(guides the customer through a device action)

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked, and my current APN is set to “internet,” and the MMSC URL for picture messages is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if these are correct, but they don’t show any obvious errors.

Should I go ahead and reset my APN settings to default just in case, or is there anything else you’d like me to check first?

Since your APN and MMSC settings appear to be set, but you’re still unable to use mobile data or send MMS, it’s a good idea to reset your APN settings to default. This can resolve hidden configuration issues that may not be obvious.

Please go ahead and reset your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Let me know once you’ve completed both steps, and we’ll check if your mobile data and MMS are working again.
(guides the customer through a device action)

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
(guides the customer through a device action)

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
(guides the customer through a device action)
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I reset my APN settings to default and rebooted my device as instructed, but unfortunately, I still can’t access mobile data—a speed test still says there’s no connection. What should I try next? I’m starting to feel a bit frustrated since this hasn’t fixed the problem yet.

Thank you for your patience and for following the steps so far. Since your SIM is active, your APN settings have been reset, and you still have no mobile data connection, I’d like to check your account and line details to see if there are any issues such as data limits being reached or other restrictions.

Please hold on while I review your data usage and plan details.
{"line_id": "L1002", "data_used_gb": "15.1", "data_limit_gb": "15.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}

I’ve checked your account, and it appears that you’ve used 15.1GB of data this billing cycle, while your plan’s monthly data limit is 15GB. This means you’ve exceeded your data allowance, which is why your mobile data and MMS are not working.

You have two options to restore your data connection:
1. Add more data to your line (up to 2GB at a time, charged at your plan’s refueling rate).
2. Change to a plan with a higher data limit.

Would you like to add more data to your line now, or would you like information about available plans with higher data limits?

Thank you for checking that for me. I’d prefer not to change my mobile data plan, but I’m willing to add 2GB of extra data so I can get everything working again. Can you help me refuel my data by 2GB?
No payment request has been made.
It looks like there’s no payment request for the data refuel yet. Could you send me a payment request for the 2GB data add-on? I’ll go ahead and complete it right away as soon as you provide it.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

A 2GB data add-on has been successfully applied to your line for $4.00. This charge will appear on your next bill.

Please try using your mobile data and sending an MMS again. If it’s still not working, try rebooting your device one more time. Let me know if you’re able to access the internet and send picture messages now!
(guides the customer through a device action)
Speed Test Result: 275.00 Mbps (Excellent). Connection is very fast.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I can now access the internet successfully—my mobile data is working and the speed is excellent. However, my messaging app still won’t send MMS messages. Is there something else I can try to get MMS working, or any troubleshooting for the messaging app itself?

Since your mobile data is now working but MMS messages still won’t send, let’s focus on troubleshooting the messaging app and related settings. Here are the next steps:

1. Please check if you can send a regular SMS (text-only) message to a single recipient—just to confirm basic messaging works.
2. If SMS works, let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to access storage and SMS. Can you check your app permissions and confirm if “storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled for your messaging app?
3. If you’re not sure how to check or change these permissions, I can guide you through the process.

Let me know the results of these checks, and if you need step-by-step instructions for checking app permissions.
(guides the customer through a device action)
App 'Messaging' not found on this phone.

I tried checking the permissions for my messaging app, but it looks like it’s not listed under the name “Messaging” on my phone. Could you let me know what to look for, or guide me on how to find the correct messaging app in my device settings? I’m not sure if it might be under a different name.

That’s a great question! The messaging app might appear under a different name depending on your device and what app you use for texting. Common names include “Messages,” “Messenger,” “SMS,” or the brand name (like “Samsung Messages” or “Google Messages”).

Here’s how you can find your default messaging app and check its permissions:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Look for apps with names like “Messages,” “Messenger,” “SMS,” “Google Messages,” or your phone brand’s messaging app (e.g., “Samsung Messages”).
4. Once you find it, tap on the app, then tap on “Permissions.”
5. Make sure both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled.

If you’re still unsure which app is your default messaging app, let me know your phone’s brand and model, and I can provide more specific instructions. Let me know what you find!
(guides the customer through a device action)
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
(guides the customer through a device action)
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.

I checked the app named "messaging" on my phone. It currently has permissions for SMS and phone, but not for storage. Should I go ahead and enable the storage permission for this app? If so, can you guide me on how to do it if I need step-by-step instructions?

Yes, please enable the storage permission for your messaging app. This permission is required for sending and receiving MMS (picture/video messages), as it allows the app to access media files on your device.

If you need step-by-step instructions, here’s how to enable storage permission:

1. Open your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and tap on your messaging app (“Messaging”).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Find “Storage” in the list and switch it ON or tap to allow access.

Once you’ve enabled storage permission, try sending an MMS again. Let me know if it works or if you need any more help!
(guides the customer through a device action)

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
(guides the customer through a device action)
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

I’ve enabled the storage permission for my messaging app. I tried sending an MMS again, and it went through successfully! Thank you so much for your help in troubleshooting and walking me through each step. Everything is working perfectly now!
I’m glad to hear that your MMS is working and everything is back to normal! If you have any more questions or need help in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a great day!
Thank you so much! I appreciate your patience and guidance throughout the process. I’ll reach out if I need anything else in the future. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###
